name: MacEacharn, Dòmhnall

attributes.attribute: turned verses of the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyám into Gaelic
published his collected work Am Fear-Ciùil in 1904

text: MacEacharn, Dòmhnall, known in English as Donald MacKechnie, lived from 1836 to 1908. He wrote Scottish Gaelic poetry but gained more notice for his prose. He was born on Jura in the Hebrides. He later settled in Edinburgh, where he joined a circle of urban Gaels. He served a newspaper trade and took an active part in Highland societies. His prose is remembered for a plain, forceful style that helped shape modern Gaelic writing. He produced a series of travel sketches and essays that recorded the life of the Highlands in his day.

okr.objective: Document the prose and verse of the Gaelic writer MacEacharn, Dòmhnall.
